about.title: About Me
about.paragraph1: I help companies adopt AI for real: I train their teams and build the custom software that puts it to work.
about.paragraph2: I'm co-founder and CTO of Tesora, Founding Engineer at Musive and an applied AI instructor in three master's programs at thePower. I take AI products from idea to production —agents, orchestration, RAG and MCP— with React, TypeScript and Node.js. What I teach in class I use in production every day, and what I learn in production ends up in class.

items.title: Tesora
items.description: AI-powered personal finance platform: connect your banks, unify your wealth, and receive intelligent advice. On web, iOS, and Android.
items.content:
Tesora is an AI-powered personal finance platform that helps you control, understand, and grow your wealth more intelligently.

Securely connect banks, investments, and crypto, visualize your real net worth (assets minus debts), and receive personalized guidance from an AI assistant that truly knows your financial situation.

Main features:
- Secure account aggregation and unified wealth with history
- Smart expense analysis and automatic categorization
- Advanced debt management with Avalanche/Snowball simulations and personalized recommendations
- Marketplace of certified financial advisors with chat and granular permissions
- Conversational AI assistant with contextual access to your data
- Savings planning with realistic scenarios and projections
- Dynamic Financial Health Score and proactive alerts

With Tesora I've learned to see my money in a completely different way: I no longer just look at scattered balances, but understand how my income, expenses, debts, and investments relate in real time. I've discovered spending patterns I used to ignore, optimized my debt payments saving thousands of euros in interest, and started making much more conscious investment decisions thanks to the simulations and context the AI provides. Most importantly, I've gone from feeling lost with finances to having a real sense of control and clear direction toward my goals.
items.tagline: AI-powered personal finance: connect your banks, unify your wealth, get intelligent advice.
items.thesis: One place to see, understand and move your money.
items.thesisNote: One app — accounts, debts, investments, and an assistant that understands the full context.
items.problem:
Existing personal-finance products tend to live at two extremes: cold aggregators that only display numbers, or generic coaching apps with no real access to your situation.

Tesora was born to close that gap — a serious aggregator with an AI assistant that actually knows your wealth, your debts, and your investments, and can reason over them in real time.

Today Tesora is a company: in October 2026 four partners incorporated TESORA Patrimonio SL, with me leading the technical side as CTO, and we're bringing the app to the App Store and Google Play.

stack.name: LLMs

stack.name: MCP

stack.name: Sentry + PostHog

items.architecture: Three pieces: a Next.js frontend that also ships as a native app through Capacitor, a modular NestJS API on PostgreSQL, and a separate admin panel. Everything runs on our own VPS behind nginx, with the API under /api on the same domain. The AI assistant works through tools over the user's data and never sees banking credentials; sensitive data is encrypted before it's stored.
items.learnings: With Tesora I've learned to see my money in a completely different way: no longer just scattered balances, but how income, expenses, debts and investments relate in real time. And technically, I've internalized that useful AI isn't the biggest model — it's the one with the right context.

items.title: Mimify
items.description: Synthetic users that browse your real site in Chromium, think out loud and tell you where they get stuck, along with the code file to change.
items.content:
Mimify is a synthetic user research team that runs locally. You tell an agent what you want to test and it sets up the study: the URL, the task, the funnel steps, the environment and who takes part. Then it launches dozens of agents, each with a person's profile (age, money, patience, distrust), that browse your actual site and answer an interview at the end.

I built it on my own, in two days with Claude Code, to test Tesora's onboarding. Since then I use it to test major changes before shipping them: 37 studies across five products.
items.eyebrow: Case study · AI agents · Side project
items.tagline: Agents with real user profiles that browse your site, get stuck where your people would and tell you why.
items.thesis: One false finding makes you distrust all the others.
items.thesisNote: The hard part isn't getting an agent to browse a website. It's making the report reliable enough to change code because of it.
items.problem:
Testing a flow with real users is slow and expensive: recruiting, scheduling, recording and drawing conclusions takes weeks, so small products almost never do it before shipping. Analytics arrive later and tell you where people drop off, but not why.

Web-browsing agents already exist, but a generic agent completing a task is nothing like a 60-year-old who distrusts the internet and opens the app on their phone. And if the report blames the site for a failure of the test itself, nobody trusts it again.

It needed something in between: as fast as an automated test, with the variety of a sample of people, and honest enough to say when a result doesn't count.

stack.name: Node.js
stack.note: Local server with just three dependencies. No framework: API, live events over SSE and a UI in plain HTML, CSS and JS.

stack.name: Playwright
stack.note: Each agent opens its own Chromium, mobile or desktop, with isolated cookies. It reads the screen as text with numbered elements, including whatever a banner covers.

stack.name: Claude Code
stack.note: The agents that set up studies (analyst, designer and profile creator) run the user's own claude headless, on their subscription and without touching their credentials.

stack.name: MCP
stack.note: MCP server and CLI to launch studies and read findings from Claude Code in another product's repo, or from CI.

stack.name: SQLite
stack.note: Native node:sqlite, one row per study and one per agent. If the server dies mid-run, the study picks up where it left off.

stack.name: Multi-LLM
stack.note: Eleven providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, Jev…). Mixing models is deliberate: lack of variety is the biggest risk with synthetic users.

features: Conversational designer: describe what you want to test and an agent reads your site and your code (read-only), picks the avatars and leaves the study ready to launch.
Avatars with real context: money, tech skills, patience and distrust from 1 to 5, a goal and a device. If a profile is missing, another agent creates it.
Live tracking of every agent: where it is, what it's thinking and whether it's moving on, stuck or giving up.
P0–P2 findings with evidence in the agent's own voice, the proposed change and the code file and line to touch, ready for Linear.
Exit interview: you can ask each agent, in first person, why it left.
Study health: visits invalidated by the test itself (anti-bot, login, tool errors) are removed from the results, and the report says so.
Pilot with one or two agents before a large study, so you don't burn 40 visits on a broken environment.
Local, staging and production profiles: in production everything is look-only, with hard limits such as paying, buying or deleting an account.
Regression across versions: the same study on every branch or commit, with a command that fails CI if completion drops below a threshold.
items.architecture: A local Node server orchestrates everything. The setup agents (project analyst, study designer and profile creator) run on Claude Code and produce a declarative config: URL, funnel steps with verifiable rules, environment and avatars. The runner splits agents across the chosen models and launches them in parallel with per-provider limits. Each agent is an observe–decide–act loop over its own Chromium: the reader turns the page into text with numbered elements, the model replies with an action validated against a JSON Schema, and a local SMTP inbox receives verification emails. At the end, an analyst cross-references journeys, interviews and the repo's code to write the findings. Everything is stored in SQLite and streamed live over SSE.
items.learnings: The first studies surfaced more bugs in the engine than in the sites: agents marking a step as done when they were actually hesitating, reports blaming the site for a failure of the test, and agents blind to charts. Each one was a false finding, and one was enough to stop believing the rest. So a good part of the work went into what you don't see: the health report, the pilot run, environment warnings and an optimism correction, because synthetic users drop off far less than real ones. Next up is calibrating it against Tesora's real analytics; until then, what it gives you is friction to review, not facts.

items.title: X-Ray
items.description: A financial-health engine that reads the banking trail of 1,286 companies and flags the ones turning months before it shows. Embat track at HackSpain 2026.
items.content:
X-Ray scores a company's financial health by reading the one thing that doesn't lie: the daily movement of its money. It was built for the Embat track at HackSpain 2026, a 36-hour hackathon at UPM's ETSIT, on a dataset of 250 corporate groups, 1,286 companies and 24 months of banking activity.

The system answers six questions: who is healthy, who is improving, who is starting to turn, whether it's a bump or a fall, why the number moved, and how many months ahead the system saw it coming.

I worked on the front end and the product, within a team of five.
items.tagline: Financial health for 1,286 companies read from their banking trail, with early warning and scenario simulation.
items.thesis: A company doesn't go under on its balance sheet. It goes under on cash.
items.thesisNote: 36 hours, five people and 24 months of bank movements to answer a single question: can money tell you how a company is doing?
items.problem:
Classic solvency models lean on annual balance sheets and accounting ratios that arrive months late. By then the decision is already made — or it's already too late.

The challenge came down to a paradox: at month 24, two companies in the dataset score almost the same — 65 and 68 — but one has been climbing from 45 and the other falling from 82. A still photo can't tell them apart; one is the best bet of the year and the other an imminent risk.

What was needed was reading the trajectory, not the portrait: separating a one-off cash squeeze from structural decline, and being able to explain every point of the score without a black box.

stack.name: Next.js
stack.note: App Router and strict TypeScript. Two audiences on one engine: Embat sees its client book, a company sees only itself.

stack.name: TypeScript
stack.note: The contract between engine and screen. If the backend changes a score factor, the front end won't compile until it knows.

stack.name: Python
stack.note: The scoring engine: continuous transforms calibrated on working-capital physics, not a classifier with no labels.

stack.name: FastAPI
stack.note: A thin REST layer with Pydantic v2 over the engine: profile, history, sector benchmark, groups and counterfactual simulation.

stack.name: DuckDB
stack.note: A 400 MB embedded columnar store. 30,000 monthly slices queried in under 10 ms, with no external infrastructure.

stack.name: Remotion
stack.note: The product video isn't a mockup: the real front-end components run inside the composition.

features: A continuous 0–100 score with exact additive decomposition: the bars add up to the change in the number, with no residual.
Early warning: catches the company that's turning while its score still looks healthy, a median of eight months ahead.
Six analytical states that separate a one-off bump from structural decline instead of firing on every bad month.
Counterfactual simulator: eight operating levers ranked by impact in points and in euros of cash freed.
Intra-group flow map inferred from a dataset that never says who pays whom, by matching amounts, dates and entities.
Holding consolidation with a contagion penalty when a subsidiary drops into critical territory.
A proactive monitor that alerts by email and Telegram with the causal breakdown of the change.
A conversational agent over an internal MCP, scoped to the company and its group.
items.architecture: The challenge CSVs are ingested into an embedded DuckDB that acts as the single source of truth. On top, a Python scoring engine processes monthly panels causally — point-in-time, no lookahead bias — and precomputes states, levers and scenarios. FastAPI exposes them over REST, and the Next.js front end paints two different products on the same API: the client book for Embat and the company profile for the company itself. The forecasting module sits apart, as a testbed for models at 1, 3 and 6 months.
items.learnings: The decision that taught me most was not training a model: the dataset had no default label, so a classifier would have meant inventing the target and dressing it up as science. Giving up ML where it didn't belong — and keeping it for forecasting, which did have a measurable time series — was worth more than any architecture.

items.title: Cosmo AI
items.description: AI productivity assistant: centralize your tasks, projects, and apps in a single personalized chat.
items.content:
Cosmo is a JARVIS-like AI productivity assistant that centralizes your tasks, projects, clients, and notes in a single web tool, currently in beta and 100% free.

Think of Cosmo as your personal mini ERP: a place where you can talk naturally with your AI assistant and, at the same time, manage your entire workflow without switching apps.

Main features:
- Intelligent conversational chat (talk to Cosmo like a teammate)
- Task management with priorities, dates, reminders, and visual tracking
- Centralized projects: all related information, tasks, notes, and clients in one place
- Personal mini ERP: integrated management of clients, projects, and notes with shared context
- Persistent memory: remembers your preferences, previous decisions, and work style
- Internet search when updated information is needed
- Integrations with your usual tools to maintain your workflow
- Experience (Exp) system and gamified statistics to track your progress
- Automatic weekly routine generator based on your priorities and goals

With this project I learned how valuable it is to connect an AI model in a real application and how it can solve different problems.
items.tagline: AI productivity assistant: centralize your tasks, projects and apps in a single personalized chat.
items.thesis: A single chat to talk, remember and manage all your work.
items.thesisNote: Your personal mini-ERP: tasks, projects, clients and notes living alongside an assistant that remembers.
items.problem:
Productivity tools are fragmented: tasks in one app, notes in another, clients in a third. Every context switch costs time and energy.

Cosmo unifies everything in one place where you talk naturally to your assistant and, at the same time, manage your workflow without switching apps.

stack.note: Strict typing: tasks, projects, clients and notes share the same contracts.

stack.note: A minimal, consistent visual system across every view of the assistant.

stack.note: Cosmo's brain: it chats, remembers context and runs actions over your workflow.

Task management with priorities, dates, reminders and visual tracking.

Personal mini-ERP with shared context across clients, projects and notes.
Persistent memory: it remembers your preferences, decisions and way of working.
Internet search when it needs up-to-date information.

items.architecture: A Next.js frontend wired to a language model with persistent memory. The assistant accesses the context of your tasks, projects and notes, and can search the internet when it needs fresh data — all without taking you out of the chat.
items.learnings: With this project I learned how valuable it is to connect an AI model to a real application, and how that lets you solve very different problems from a single conversational interface.

items.title: BTC Tracker
items.description: Bitcoin purchase calculator and tracker to monitor average price, holdings, and real-time P&L.
items.content:
BTC Average Price is a web app designed to log and analyze Bitcoin buy/sell transactions with a focus on one key metric: your real average buy price in USD.

The app provides a clear overview of your position, shows unrealized profit/loss, and helps you make better decisions before selling.

Key features:
- Automatic average buy price calculation
- Real-time metrics: current value, BTC holdings, total investment, and unrealized P&L
- Live BTC price with periodic updates
- Full transaction history with edit, delete, and CSV export options
- Add transactions in 3 modes: manual entry, generic CSV upload, and exchange importer
- Dedicated importers for Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, and Revolut
- Automatic currency conversion to USD to normalize real cost basis
- Sell simulator to estimate proceeds, cost basis, and profit/loss before executing a trade
- Purchase chart to visualize entry evolution and average cost over time
- Market sentiment widget (Fear & Greed Index)
- Google authentication or guest mode, with user-based data persistence in Firebase
- PWA support to install the app on desktop or mobile devices

With this project, I worked on a real crypto personal finance use case, integrating market data, multi-currency normalization, and heterogeneous data imports into a simple end-user experience.
items.tagline: Bitcoin purchase calculator and tracker for average price, holdings and real-time P&L.
items.thesis: Your real average price and Bitcoin P&L, in real time.
items.thesisNote: Log every buy, normalize currencies to USD and know exactly what your position is worth.
items.problem:
Anyone stacking Bitcoin over time loses track of their real average price and returns. Spreadsheets don't normalize currencies or import exchange activity.

BTC Tracker focuses on one key metric —your real average buy price in USD— and combines it with live metrics to decide better before selling.

items.architecture: A Next.js app with PWA support, per-user data persisted in Firebase and a live BTC price. The exchange-specific importers normalize currencies to USD so the average cost reflects reality.
items.learnings: With this project I worked through a real personal-crypto-finance case: integrating market data, normalizing multiple currencies and importing heterogeneous sources, all inside a simple experience for the end user.

items.title: TalkBook
items.description: Personal reading library with chat about your books, built with React, Supabase and a mobile-first experience.
items.content:
TalkBook is a web application for readers who want to have their personal library always at hand and be able to talk about what they read.

You can save the books you're reading or have read, with their covers, authors, descriptions, and ISBN, and keep your progress organized in a single place. You can also search for new titles using the Google Books API and easily add books to your library.

The most special feature of TalkBook is the book chat: you can open a conversation centered on a specific title and talk about its content, key ideas, questions, or reflections, always keeping the context of that book.

Main features:
- Personal library of read and reading books
- Book cards with cover, author, description, and basic information
- Google Books search integration
- Ability to quickly add books to your collection
- Chat associated with each book to talk about what you're reading
- Mobile-first interface with bottom navigation and clean design

With this project I was able to explore how to design a richer reading digital experience, where not only do you save your books, but you can also talk about them and turn your library into an active reflection space.
items.tagline: Personal reading library with a chat about your books, built with React, Supabase and a mobile-first experience.
items.thesis: Your library — but built to talk to your books.
items.thesisNote: Save what you read and open a conversation focused on each title, without losing context.
items.problem:
We tend to save what we read in dead lists we never revisit. Reading is left without a space to reflect on its ideas.

TalkBook turns your library into an active place: you organize your books and, above all, talk to each one about its content, key ideas and your questions.

items.title: Roundtable
items.description: AI-powered thinking tool: configure a personal roundtable of historical and modern thinkers to debate ideas and improve decision-making.
items.content:
Roundtable is a thinking and decision-making tool inspired by a practice described by Napoleon Hill: sitting with a personal council of trusted references to debate ideas and gain clarity.

The app allows you to create your own roundtable of historical and modern figures — philosophers, entrepreneurs, scientists, and leaders — each represented by an AI agent trained on their mental models and decision frameworks.

Through an orchestrated multi-agent debate, agents don't just respond to the user, they challenge each other, surface trade-offs, and expose blind spots.

Main features:
- Configurable roundtables with multiple AI agents
- Distinct mental models and perspectives per agent
- Orchestrated debates and moderated discussions
- Decision-focused conversations, not generic answers
- Designed for clarity, reflection, and better thinking
items.tagline: AI thinking tool: assemble a roundtable of historical and modern thinkers to debate ideas and decide better.
items.thesis: A council of brilliant minds debating your decision.
items.thesisNote: Agents that don't just answer you: they challenge each other and surface your blind spots.
items.problem:
Making good decisions alone is hard: we lack perspectives and fall into blind spots.

Inspired by a practice described by Napoleon Hill, Roundtable seats you with a personal council of thinkers —represented by AI agents— who debate your dilemma from different mental frameworks.

items.learnings: Building Roundtable taught me to design multi-agent systems where the value isn't a single answer but the contrast of perspectives. Orchestrating agents that challenge each other —and keeping the debate focused on the decision— is as much a design problem as a prompting one.

items.title: Evolvio Website
items.description: Website for the digital development agency Evolvio.
items.content:
Evolvio is a digital innovation agency that designs and develops custom solutions for SMEs and companies: websites that convert, AI automations, and online presence strategies that drive real growth (up to x10, according to their claim).

They specialize in transforming typical problems ('your website doesn't sell', time wasted on repetitive tasks, inefficient management) into competitive advantages through custom development and intelligent technology.

Main features:
- Modern web development: responsive sites, optimized for conversion (UX, powerful CTAs, on-page SEO, behavior analysis)
- AI automations and integrations: smart integrations to save hours and improve customer experience
- Online presence and digital marketing (coming soon expanded): visibility, qualified traffic, and digital branding
- Professional websites from €500 (offer): responsive, basic SEO, hosting + SSL 1 year, 24/7 support and high availability
- Clear iterative process: Discovery → Strategy → Implementation → Continuous optimization
- Focus on measurable results: more visits, more sales, 99.99% online, secure and fast solutions
- Real social proof: testimonials and case studies from clients like Suicalsa, Tierra de Fuego, RCI, or Motoreciclajesp

With Evolvio I've learned to see digital presence not as an expense, but as a direct growth lever. Understanding that a well-made website (that actually sells and isn't just 'there') combined with smart automations can free up valuable time and multiply results without needing huge internal teams. It has changed my way of thinking about digital projects: less 'make it pretty' and more 'make it generate money and efficiency'.

Many SMBs' websites are 'just there' but don't sell. Evolvio needed a site that communicated its offer —websites that convert and AI automations— and that was, in itself, proof of its work.

items.title: Zentunes
items.description: Web player of relaxing sounds for working, sleeping, or relaxing.
items.content:
ZenTunes is a high-quality relaxing sounds web player, designed to help you focus, relax, or sleep with ambiances like rain, forest, waves, or coffee shop.

It's a side project created by Hugo in 24 hours as a quick demo, designed to be simple, beautiful, and effective.

Main features:
- High-quality ambient sounds for background (rain, wind, nature, coffee, etc.)
- Mix multiple sounds simultaneously with individual volume control
- Background playback (you can continue browsing or working with the sound active)
- Minimalist and intuitive interface: choose a sound and start listening in seconds
- Light and fast: no installation required, works directly in the browser

With ZenTunes I've learned how valuable it is to have a simple, distraction-free tool to improve focus or disconnect. It has helped me create personalized sound environments that really work for me (for example, soft rain + coffee background) and I've discovered that sometimes fewer options and more simplicity is exactly what I need to focus or relax without complications.
items.tagline: Web player of relaxing sounds for working, sleeping or relaxing.
items.thesis: Fewer options, more focus. Ambient sound in seconds.
items.thesisNote: A side project built in 24 hours: simple, beautiful and effective, with nothing extra.
items.problem:
Ambient-sound apps tend to be overloaded with options and friction.

ZenTunes is the opposite: you pick a sound —or mix several, each with its own volume— and start focusing or relaxing in seconds, without installing anything.

items.learnings: With ZenTunes I learned how valuable a simple, distraction-free tool can be for focus. I discovered that sometimes fewer options and more simplicity is exactly what I need to concentrate or unwind.

comunicacion.title: Communication & Teaching
comunicacion.subtitle: I can build… and I can explain it. Teaching, podcast and video: what sets me apart beyond code.

items.title: Instructor at thePower
items.tagline: Instructor across three of thePower's master's programs. Mostly on AI: agents, Claude Code, MCP, N8N, and Codex.
items.thesis: I teach people to build with AI for real — not to copy prompts.
items.thesisNote: Three programs at once, from non-technical profiles to senior developers.
items.intro:
Most AI training stops at calling an API and little more. The real jump —agents, Claude Code, MCP, and automation with AI inside the workflow— is exactly what companies need and almost nobody teaches.

At thePower I taught across three master's programs at once, with very different students in front of me: business profiles who want to build a product with AI, developers who need to master agentic development, and people learning to code from scratch. I've taught React and web development fundamentals, but the weight of what I taught was AI: on top of the classes, I recorded the Claude Code and Codex specializations and ran the live agentic-development sessions.

Teaching at that scale is what forced me to hold my own opinion: repeating what some YouTube video says doesn't hold up when you have to answer a senior engineer live, someone who's taking this straight to production.
craft: Applied AI: taking models into real products, not demos.
Claude Code and Codex specializations: professional workflow, permissions, skills, MCP, and Git.
Live agentic-development sessions: a multi-agent productivity assistant wired up through MCP, built over four sessions.
Process automation with N8N, with AI inside the workflow.
React and web development fundamentals — the base everything above stands on.
items.takeaway: This is what earns me authority to talk about AI outside the classroom: talks and tailored training for companies that need to adopt AI and don't know where to start. If I can take a student from zero to building agents, I can sit down with a team and tell them what makes sense in their case and what's just hype.

items.title: La Última Versión
items.tagline: A podcast by Hugo and Juanma on AI, finance and the digital future. 14 episodes, one a week.
items.thesis: AI, finance and the digital future. No hype.
items.thesisNote: More an audit of tomorrow than hype: every episode crossed at least two axes of the tech conversation.
items.intro:
There's too much noise and hype around AI and finance, and too little thoughtful conversation.

La Última Versión was born to cross AI, technology and money without the hype: a podcast that explained the real impact of innovation on our present, with a direct tone. And for me it was where I trained, week after week, communicating complex ideas to an audience.

The format ran on two voices: Juanma brought software and science, I brought business and strategy. I scripted and structured every conversation so complex ideas would land, and each show yielded vertical clips with the highlights.

We wrapped it up after 14 episodes. It had a finite horizon, and much of its value was in the process of learning to make a podcast.

episodes.title: Will we live forever?, the habits that make you rich, and whether getting rich is luck or skill.
Clever vs. intelligent?, standing out in the age of AI, and the decline of IQ.

items.takeaway: With La Última Versión I bring something beyond code to my portfolio: learning to communicate complex ideas with clarity and consistency. That ability to explain technology is precisely what opened the door to teaching.

items.title: YouTube Channel
items.tagline: Vlogs on entrepreneurship, building in public, lifestyle, and a bit of AI.
items.thesis: Communicating ideas and building an audience, camera in hand.
items.thesisNote: My communication lab: where I train scripting, on-camera presence and consistency.
items.intro:
Knowing about technology isn't enough if you can't convey it. I needed my own space to train what sets me apart most: telling ideas clearly and sustaining it over time.

This channel is that lab. It's not a tech channel: it's long-form vlogs of 8 to 15 minutes, one topic per video, mixing building in public (Tesora and my projects), lifestyle and personal development, and a bit of AI.
craft: Scripting and narrative structure for each video.
Presence and naturalness in front of the camera.
My own filming and editing, end to end.
items.takeaway: Communicating well is a skill you build by publishing. That practice in front of a camera is, literally, part of what opened the door to teaching at thePower.
